2026-08-19T03:25:37.7382946Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7383324Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7383903Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7384416Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7384830Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7385335Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7386908Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7388603Z >
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7390911Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7393243Z >
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7406259Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7407100Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7407300Z ### How to Use
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7407557Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7408282Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7409020Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7409197Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7409809Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7410541Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7411150Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7411354Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7411622Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7412160Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7412711Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7413499Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7414931Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7415681Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7415896Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7416574Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7417437Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7418016Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7418720Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7418929Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7419420Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7420028Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7420565Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7421420Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7422123Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7422331Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7422605Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7423022Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7424787Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7426352Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7426530Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7426981Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7427831Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7428654Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7428963Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7429443Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7430435Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7431237Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7431703Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7431907Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7432655Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7433544Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7433939Z ```bash
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7434657Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7435533Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7436240Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7436678Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7437078Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7437872Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7438417Z ```
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7438616Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7438828Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7439634Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7440598Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7441546Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7442539Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7443900Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7444480Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7444660Z ### Notes
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7444887Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7445504Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7446901Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7448162Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7449399Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7450589Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7451705Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7452664Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7453375Z </mcp-clis>

2026-08-19T03:25:37.7467077Z 
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7467448Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7468316Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7469160Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7470026Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7470872Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7471661Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7472505Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7473357Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7474333Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7475198Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
2026-08-19T03:25:37.7475851Z table.
